doc.title: Dave Rivello interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rochester, New York, January 11, 2012

title: Choosing permanent members and subs for his band
summary: He vets players musically and socially because one bad apple harms a twelve-piece band.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: Have you had to try different sidemen to find the people you like?

I’ve been fortunate that I do that work on the front end so that I’m very careful about who I ask, especially to be a permanent member of my band. And so generally there’ll be subs that I call, good players, and I kind of feel them out and watch their interaction when they’re subbing with the band, with the rest of the band. Because for me — the musical

ability obviously is the most important thing. But a very close second is how they act. Because one bad apple, especially my band is a twelve-piece band. One guy who doesn’t interact well with the others really changes the picture in a negative way. So I’m very careful about, even somebody who has subbed, if there’s an open chair permanently, who is going to come into the band and be that permanent player, I think long and hard about that every time before I make that final decision. So fortunately because of doing it that way I haven’t really had any issues with that.
Are you talking about interacting musically and otherwise?

Musically and socially, their attitude, their demeanor, all of those things. You know one guy who thinks that he’s better than somebody else is going to really change the picture, and then all of a sudden my regular guys are like, “Oh by the way Dave, yeah, I can’t make Thursday’s gig” — because it’s not fun anymore for them, so the thing that can happen is it starts falling apart. So as long as they know for me as a leader, because anybody with a big band I think — I forget who it was, somebody famous said “Whenever you see a big band playing somebody’s losing money.” So these guys are not playing for big money. They’re doing it because they love to do it and they’re having fun doing it. So if one element makes it unfun for them, not fun, then all of a sudden there’s a whole other world that opens up that I have to take care of. So by trying to take care of that on the front end and being careful about who I select and who I ask, then I’ve not had really trouble in that way.
